teacher_walkthrough: We are constructing a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram to display the weekly snowfall in centimetres for 11 weeks in Dados and Linva.

Step 1: Determine the stems.
The lowest value is 0 (in Linva) and the highest is 42 (in Dados).
Using tens digits gives stems: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

Step 2: Order data for Dados (left-hand side):
Stem 0: 6, 8 $\implies$ leaves $8, 6$ (increasing right-to-left)
Stem 1: 10, 10, 12, 15, 16 $\implies$ leaves $6, 5, 2, 0, 0$
Stem 2: 22, 28 $\implies$ leaves $8, 2$
Stem 3: 36 $\implies$ leaf $6$
Stem 4: 42 $\implies$ leaf $2$

Step 3: Order data for Linva (right-hand side):
Stem 0: 0, 2, 9 $\implies$ leaves $0, 2, 9$ (increasing left-to-right)
Stem 1: 10, 11, 12, 15, 16 $\implies$ leaves $0, 1, 2, 5, 6$
Stem 2: none
Stem 3: 32, 36 $\implies$ leaves $2, 6$
Stem 4: 40 $\implies$ leaf $0$

Step 4: Provide a clear key:
$$\text{Key: } 6 \mid 3 \mid 2 \text{ means } 36\text{ cm in Dados and } 32\text{ cm in Linva}$$

hints: Dados has $n = 11$ weekly snowfall values. Find the position of the median: $\frac{11 + 1}{2} = 6\text{th}$ value.
List Dados values in increasing order: 6, 8, 10, 10, 12, 15, 16, 22, 28, 36, 42.
The median is the 6th value ($15$ cm).
The lower quartile $Q_1$ is the 3rd value ($10$ cm) and the upper quartile $Q_3$ is the 9th value ($28$ cm). Calculate $\text{IQR} = 28 - 10$.
walkthrough:
Find the median:
$$\text{Position of median} = \dfrac{11 + 1}{2} = 6\text{th value} \implies \text{Median} = 15\text{ cm}$$

Find the quartiles:
$$Q_1 = 3\text{rd value} = 10\text{ cm}$$
$$Q_3 = 9\text{th value} = 28\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 28 - 10 = 18\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Identifies the 6th value as median = 15 cm, lower quartile as 10 cm, and upper quartile as 28 cm.

teacher_walkthrough: We need to find the median and interquartile range for the weekly snowfall in Dados.

Step 1: Write the 11 snowfall values of Dados in increasing order:
$$6, \; 8, \; 10, \; 10, \; 12, \; 15, \; 16, \; 22, \; 28, \; 36, \; 42$$

Step 2: Find the median ($Q_2$):
With $n = 11$, the median position is:
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{11 + 1}{2} = 6\text{th value}$$
The 6th value is $15$ cm.

Step 3: Find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) and upper quartile ($Q_3$):
The 5 values below the median are $6, 8, 10, 10, 12$. The middle of these is the 3rd value overall:
$$Q_1 = 10\text{ cm}$$
The 5 values above the median are $16, 22, 28, 36, 42$. The middle of these is the 9th value overall:
$$Q_3 = 28\text{ cm}$$

Step 4: Compute the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 28 - 10 = 18\text{ cm}$$

hints: Compare the central tendencies: compare the median of Dados ($15$ cm) with the median of Linva ($12$ cm).
Compare the spreads: calculate the IQR for Linva ($32 - 9 = 23$ cm) and compare with the IQR for Dados ($18$ cm).
State one contextual statement for central tendency (average snowfall) and one for spread (variability).
walkthrough:
Comparison of central tendency:
The median weekly snowfall in Dados ($15\text{ cm}$) is higher than in Linva ($12\text{ cm}$), meaning that snowfall in Dados is on average higher.

Comparison of spread / variability:
The interquartile range for Linva ($32 - 9 = 23\text{ cm}$) is greater than for Dados ($18\text{ cm}$), showing that the weekly snowfall in Linva is more spread out and varies more than in Dados.

ai_rubric.Comparing Distributions: Compares central tendency (median for Dados is higher) and spread (IQR for Linva is higher / varies more) in context.

teacher_walkthrough:
We are given for Linva:
$$\text{Median} = 12\text{ cm}, \quad Q_1 = 9\text{ cm}, \quad Q_3 = 32\text{ cm} \implies \text{IQR} = 32 - 9 = 23\text{ cm}$$
And from part (b) for Dados:
$$\text{Median} = 15\text{ cm}, \quad \text{IQR} = 18\text{ cm}$$

Step 1: Compare central tendency (medians).
Since the median for Dados ($15$ cm) is greater than the median for Linva ($12$ cm):
Statement: On average, the weekly snowfall in Dados is higher than in Linva.

Step 2: Compare spread (interquartile ranges).
Since the IQR for Linva ($23$ cm) is greater than the IQR for Dados ($18$ cm):
Statement: The weekly snowfall in Linva is more spread out (varies more) than in Dados.
